summary: Service account name-hash collision during automated provisioner blocks GCP env bootstrap
description:
Issue summary:
Automated environment bootstrap (infra/provisioner) fails when creating a service account because the generated account_id collides with an existing account_id in another project.

Impact:
- New private/development GCP environments fail to finish onboarding; terraform/apply aborts with 409 errors.
- Affects Dedicated/Private onboarding pipelines that rely on deterministic account naming.
- Blocks a small number of envs in eu-west and us-east while we investigate.

Environment:
- Component: infra/auto-provisioner (terraform wrapper + custom python helper)
- Affected projects: redwood-private-eu-west-003 (example), redwood-dedicated-eu-west-001 (example)
- Regions observed: eu-west, us-east
- When reproducing: staging and prod-like CI runners invoking provisioning workflow

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run the onboarding job for a new environment using the standard pipeline (provisioner v2.4.1).
2) Provisioner calls helper to compute service account account_id using deterministic hash(account_name + env_seed) truncated to 12 chars.
3) Terraform applies google_service_account resource and fails with a 409 response from IAM.

Observed behavior:
- Terraform error: "googleapi: Error 409: Service account with the given accountId already exists, alreadyExists"
- Provisioner log shows two different projects resolving to the same account_id (e.g. redwood-llm-provisioner-9f2b7c1a).
- IAM audit log shows creation attempt in target project followed by a duplicate creation attempt that resolves to existing SA in a different project id.

Expected behavior:
- Provisioner should generate unique account_ids across projects to avoid collisions; onboarding should succeed.

Logs/Artifacts:
- Provisioner log snippet (CI run 2026-03-10T14:22Z): "create service account redwood-llm-provisioner-9f2b7c1a -> 409 alreadyExists"
- gcloud IAM audit: principal: infra-provisioner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com attempted createServiceAccount; response: AlreadyExists
- Terraform plan shows new google_service_account resource with account_id = "redwood-llm-provisioner-9f2b7c1a"

Temporary workaround:
- Manually pick a unique suffix and re-run apply (team: infra-ops).
- Short term: modify pipeline to append CI_BUILD_ID to account_id for new envs to guarantee uniqueness (applied to two failing envs, success verified).

Notes on scope:
- This is not a GCP platform outage; it is a deterministic-naming collision inside our provisioning tool.
- Risk: If left, will continue to intermittently block environment bootstrap for new projects created with colliding seeds.
environment: prod-like CI; also reproduces in staging
comments: 2026-03-10 15:04 - Aisha Patel: Initial report and logs attached. CI run 782 failed when creating SA; looks like deterministic suffix collision. Assigning to infra oncall.

2026-03-10 17:12 - Marco Li: Confirmed reproduce in staging. Hash truncation (to 12 chars) is the culprit — two different env seeds hashed to same prefix. Temporarily patched pipeline to include CI_BUILD_ID; re-ran failing job and it succeeded. Need a permanent fix.

investigation_notes: Checked terraform apply logs and IAM admin audit logs in Cloud Logging to correlate project IDs to the 409 errors.

Reproduced locally: deterministic_hash('redwood-llm-provisioner','env-seed-abc') truncated to 12 returned same token as hash('redwood-llm-provisioner','env-seed-xyc') due to truncation and collision in algorithm (birthday paradox at truncated length).

GCP error message: 'AlreadyExists: Service account with the given accountId already exists.' The API returns the project_id that owns the existing account in the audit entry — used this to enumerate collisions.

Provisioner code path: provisioner/helpers/sa_namer.py uses sha256 -> hex -> first 12 chars. Collision rate estimated ~1e-6 per new env, but deterministic seeds increase likelihood between certain env names.
CI workaround applied: append CI_BUILD_ID or timestamp to account_id when invoked from CI; manual remediation applied to two blocked envs and verified success.
Security review: no cross-project binding automatically granted because of collision; create call fails, so no credential leakage.
resolution: Work in progress — root cause identified (hash truncation collision). Short-term mitigations applied (CI append fallback). Next steps: merge PR to change account_id algo to include project id + longer hash (24 chars), add pre-flight collision check against org-wide service account index, and add alerting for 409 createServiceAccount events. Targeted rollout: provisioner v2.5.0.
resolution_notes: PRs: infra/pull/7345 modifies SA naming; provisioner/pull/502 adds collision tests and preflight check. Plan to deploy to staging 2026-03-18 and to prod 2026-03-22 after smoke tests.
